correctness.rationale: Parseval and H_t selfadjoint semigroup give S(t)=diag(H_2t(v,v)) exactly. The six explicit Laplacian eigenspaces have dimensions summing 18k and diagonal spectral-projector weights summing one at both kinds of vertices. This yields exact two-eigenvalue frame spectrum. Symbolic factorization Δ=x^8(1-x)Q_k(x)/(40k) and transformed polynomial coefficients are independently checked. For integer k≥1 the transformed coefficients have exactly one sign change (positive constant and negative leading), so Descartes and IVT give one simple positive root mapped to x∈(0,1) and exactly one finite positive crossing. Endpoint signs establish strict order elsewhere; asymptotics from root equation. Direct matrix-exponential and rational checks corroborate but do not replace general proof.

evidence: Ghandehari–Guillot–Hollingsworth provide a generic all-graph sharp frame-bound formula for arbitrary translated windows.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general theorem determines bounds conditional on heat diagonals, but it does not imply that the diagonals cross at one positive time for the particular growing family. The known all-time sufficient hypotheses do not include these irregular graphs. A stronger all-graph classification of isolated heat-diagonal collisions was not identified.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior results supply the generic relationship S(t)=diag exp(-2tL) but no automatic equality for an irregular graph. The proof determines the full Laplacian spectral projectors of a new explicit graph family and proves a unique positive collision via a polynomial with one sign change under a Möbius transform. Thus generic prior formulas do not logically imply the new quantified family theorem without these new calculations; the theorem would be covered if an earlier heat-centrality theorem explicitly gives the same family and crossing.

General diagonal criteria state equivalence, not existence, uniqueness or root location. Risk remains that a spectral graph centrality paper could implicitly prove the same crossing.

value.rationale: An infinite, connected and strictly irregular graph family with a single isolated finite heat-time exact tightness shows that regularity-based all-time sufficient conditions are not necessary at a particular heat time. Sharp time-dependent frame spectrum and an exact unique crossing provide a meaningful algebraic counterexample and quantitative design benchmark, rather than routine restatement of general diagonal bounds.
